name: Bahamas
summary_text: The Bahamas demands real caution. Same-sex conduct decriminalised in 1991; tourism-dependent economy with extensive international exposure; no LGR; documented social hostility but no criminalisation and no police-targeting pattern.

sources.claim_summary: ILGA World Database jurisdiction page for the Bahamas: documents the legal status of same-sex conduct (decriminalised by the 1991 sexual-offences law, with a higher same-sex age of consent) and gender recognition.

sources.title: Fred Mitchell Uncensored.Com For June 2001
sources.claim_summary: NOTE: This is a 2001 Bahamian political newsletter (Fred Mitchell) with general political content; its LGBT relevance (the 2001 referendum debate on banning same-sex marriage discrimination) is not visible in the retrieved text.

The Tribune (April 2016): 'Transgender plea for rights' - Bahamas Transgender, Intersex United (BTIU) launched the 'Bahamian Trans Lives Matter' campaign calling for equal access to healthcare, education and employment without discrimination, during the gender-equality referendum debate; spokesperson Alexus D'Marco described the constraints of socially accepted behaviour in The Bahamas.

sources.title: Gay Law Net ®™ | Laws | Bahamas | BS
sources.claim_summary: GayLawNet Bahamas laws page: consensual same-sex sex lawful at 18 (Sexual Offences and Domestic Violence Act 1991, with life imprisonment for sex with a same-sex minor); in 1998 the National Security Minister stated the military, prison service and police do not discriminate based on sexual orientation.

The Tribune (May 2017): an American visitor was beaten at Bahamas Junkanoo Carnival, alleging he was 'targeted and beat up' because he is gay; he sought hate-crime charges and planned to sue - documents violence against an LGBT visitor.
